## Clean, bounded live-update flow

- Fleet telemetry is persisted exactly as before, but the server now publishes
  one unit WebSocket invalidation for all accepted VPS samples in each fixed
  15-second window. Raw per-VPS telemetry notices are not serialized to the
  browser. A connected browser performs one live snapshot for that aggregate
  invalidation; disconnected sessions retain the existing bounded fallback and
  reconnect recovery.
- Job output changes are published as one sorted, deduplicated set of dirty job
  IDs per fixed five-second window. The selected Job Details panel refreshes
  targets, output, and comparison as one single-flight group, keeps the current
  evidence visible while it loads, and collapses an in-flight wave to one
  trailing refresh.
- Job History no longer reloads its full newest-first dataset for terminal
  events. Existing loaded rows update in place without returning the operator
  to page 1; newly created rows remain behind the existing manual Refresh
  action.

## Reliability

- PostgreSQL runtime-configuration CAS failures now await transaction rollback
  before returning, so an immediate reviewed retry cannot encounter a lock
  left briefly behind by the failed attempt.
- Per-target progress no longer emits a misleading `job_finished` event while
  the aggregate job is still queued or running.

## Compatibility

- The server and frontend must be deployed together because the public live
  stream now carries aggregate `fleet_telemetry_invalidated` and
  `job_details_invalidated` messages instead of raw per-VPS telemetry/output
  notices. Agent and gateway command protocols, stored data, and REST workflows
  are unchanged.
- Database migrations remain exactly `0001`–`0009` with unchanged checksums.
- v0.4.3 supersedes the cancelled, unpublished v0.4.2 release candidate.
